name: Big Dip O’ruby
lede: Big Dip O’ruby is a dark, slightly brownish red named for the gem ruby, and one of the rarest named colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A gem-stone red
sections.body:
Our library files Big Dip O’ruby as a pigment-and-mineral word, taking its name from ruby, the deep red gem, with Wikipedia citing Crayola as the source of the swatch [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system would class a match to it as a deep red, about 6.6 units of ΔE from that block's center [1].

The nearest everyday name on file is [[raspberry]], 4.3 units away, with [[cranberry]] listed as its closer informal neighbor; a separate library entry, Red-Violet (Color Wheel), sits only 2.3 units off as a near-duplicate swatch under a different name [1]. Measured in LCH terms it is dark and richly saturated: lightness 36, chroma 52, hue 14 degrees, just on the red side of magenta [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings finds a close match to Big Dip O’ruby in only 7, as photographed, making it rarer than almost every other name we track [2]. The earliest is Vincenzo Frediani's *The Adoration of the Christ Child*, from about 1485, and the fullest is François Clouet's *A Lady in Her Bath* of 1571, where it covers about 17 percent of the canvas [2]. A match also turns up in Ernst Ludwig Kirchner's *Two Girls under an Umbrella* of 1910 and in undated Indian and Chinese works in the archive, so the small count spans five centuries rather than clustering in one [2].
